memo.verdict: Bullish; progress to Early-Stage; conviction low, a working hypothesis. The park rule does not bite: management C (RA 3, E 1, BB 4), business quality B (E 2, BB 2), predictability C (RA 8, E 2, BB 4), trackability B (RA 7, E 2, BB 4); no D or F on the four gates. The case clears the eighteen-month 20 percent bar at 873p with about 2 percent to spare on a blended multiple (the blended value of 1,166p discounted at 20 percent a year is 887p) and clears the three-year bar only below about 786p or on the cleared branch. A starter position at today's price is a bet on the Q4 2026 US scanner print; the position earns its full size only once two further quarters print above 10 percent. Invalidation: a Q4 2026 scanner print below 10 percent turns 'Investment Thesis' to C and 'Investment Case' to D; a quarter in which US shipment growth exceeds scanner growth by more than 5 points invalidates the clearing reading outright.
case: Thesis. Fevertree is an oversold, category-leading premium mixer brand whose self-made cause for concern is starting to clear: it licensed its largest region to Molson Coors in January 2025 while its margins sat at a trough, and the H1 2026 results gave the first hard evidence that the new model grows. At 873p the shares pay 19.3x 24-month-forward earnings, the 7th percentile of their own five-year range, for a business at its trough margin; on the record's modal path they return about 21 percent a year over eighteen months, and the case turns on whether US consumer takeaway keeps growing above 10 percent through 2027 under a partner the company does not control.

The change is internal, the largest in the company's history, and executed. The US licence converted the largest region into a royalty stream with contractually guaranteed minimum profits 2026 to 2030, took working capital and the local profit and loss off Fevertree's books, brought 400 distributors and 500,000 accounts, and onshores production by 2027 to remove freight and tariffs. The company became a capital returner (£160m over 2025 and 2026). Five of twelve internal forces are strong (strategy change B; perimeter change B; new products B; balance-sheet utilisation B; shareholder returns A), more than the framework's three; no red flag (no caretaker chief executive, no debt-funded buyback, no presentation-only transformation). There is no chief executive change (F) and no guidance raise (D; FY2026 held; the 15 percent margin target withdrawn in Q2 2024; the only new mid-term number the £100m free-cash-flow floor). The propagation: choices (the licence) into actions (the subsidiary sale, the campaign, the buybacks) into operating metrics and one half-year of statements.

The external forces net to neutral and lean against the core occasion (RA 1, E 1, BB 1: C). Demand C: the core spirits-mixing occasion contracts (UK gin in structural decline; UK on-trade about 35 percent below 2019; US spirits value -0.6 percent; tonic 53 percent of sales) while premium adult soft drinks and moderation formats grow (47 percent of sales beyond tonic, +13 percent); the company's growth is share and distribution, not category. The company's own cycle B (turning, dated to H1 2026). Supply side B (hedged to 2028; freight back to historic levels; carbon dioxide on biomass). Political and regulatory D (the levy, the deposit scheme, tariffs). Macroeconomic D (UK inflation 3.1 percent in August 2026; US consumer confidence 90.8 in July 2026; a premium product sold in bars carries more of it than a staple). Competition C (easing in the US premium tier, where Fevertree and Q Mixers hold nearly 90 percent and Q Mixers is losing share; tightening in the UK, where Schweppes and London Essence take share; private label 38 to 45 percent in Spain and the Netherlands). Disruption C (ready-to-drink cocktails and GLP-1 against; draught and cans for; the ready-to-drink wave cresting). Currency a translation nuisance, not a force.
counter_case: At its strongest: the H1 2026 numbers are a false friend, and 19x is not cheap for what is left. The 16 percent July and August scanner rate is pipeline fill and marketing-bought trial that coincides with the first national television campaign, on the half of the US business that can be seen; the invisible half, the on-trade where the brand's cachet was built, is being commoditised by beer representatives who cannot sell a premium mixer to a cocktail bar, and a former US manager warns they lack the expertise. The guaranteed minimum profits to 2030 make the royalty look fine while the franchise stagnates beneath it, and the floor delays the reading of the franchise until the joint operation's margin is disclosed. The profit-share caps the group margin near 17 percent for good, so the 30 percent margins of history and the multiples paid for them are gone. The UK core shrinks with gin whatever the weather does in a given half; core tonic was flat in H1 2026 only with favourable weather, the on-trade is 35 percent below 2019 and squeezed by costs, and management has deflected the on-trade question. The £5m a year of exceptionals is the cost of running the business, not a transition item; it has recurred for three years. Management is paid on revenue and insulated from margin, missed for three years, dismissed the levy before provisioning for it, and runs a business through three people with no successor. Net cash has halved and the buyback pace cannot continue without leverage. Redburn calls 18 percent US consensus growth unachievable and models a stall at 6 percent; three of ten visible brokers are Hold and one is Sell at 700p; the June 2026 analysis of competing hypotheses gave the false-friend profile zero disconfirmations against nine for the bull case. A 3 to 4 percent grower with a 15 percent margin ceiling, four company-specific concerns, three exogenous headwinds, a D on broad mediocrity and a partner-controlled engine is not cheap at 19x when beer peers are at 10x to 15x, staples at about 17x, and the same shares are 24x to 25x on a one-year-forward footing. In the uncleared branch the shares lose 18.3 percent over eighteen months; the individually tolerable weaknesses become fatal together because every one bites at once and there is no second engine. On the setup, the case is really a 'Major CfC Clearing' or 'Trough on Trough' that has not capitulated, so the right action is to wait for the capitulation a false-friend outcome would bring and buy lower. On the case, a C with a D on broad mediocrity (17 of 39 scoped attributes at C) is exactly the case of too many Cs the framework says to reject, whatever the multiple says.

The record's concessions: the margin ceiling (its path stops at 15.5 percent); the UK (flat at best); the opacity of the profit bridge; the brevity of the evidence (one half-year; two months of scanner data on half a region); the C-count; that the price has not capitulated and a scanner stall would produce that capitulation; that in the uncleared branch the shares lose 18 percent; and that no segment can be shown to cover the enterprise value at any multiple, because the UK profit pool and the US floor are not disclosed.
triggers: - US off-trade scanner growth (Circana), monthly: current 16 percent (July and August 2026); modal 10 to 12 percent through FY2027; Alarm below 10 percent for a quarter; Invalidate below 6 percent for two quarters, or shipments above scanner by more than 5 points for a quarter. A Q4 2026 print below 10 percent turns 'Investment Thesis' to C and 'Investment Case' to D and removes the only two Bs among the Building Blocks.

- US shipment growth against scanner growth (the false-friend diagnostic): Alarm shipments above scanner for a quarter; Invalidate by more than 5 points for a quarter. Also the record's stated point of changing its mind on the thesis, alongside scanner growth reverting below 10 percent by Q1 2027.
- US brand revenue growth, constant currency: current +11 percent (H1 2026); modal +11 to +12 percent; Alarm below 8 percent at FY2026; Invalidate single digits in FY2027.
- Onshoring: cans autumn 2026, glass 2027; Alarm glass guided past 2027; Invalidate full onshoring guided past Q2 2027.

- Group adjusted EBITDA margin: current 10.9 percent (H1 2026); guidance-equivalent 12.4 percent FY2026; modal 12.3, 14.3, 15.5 percent; consensus 12.5, 15.0, 16.6 percent; Alarm below 12 percent for FY2026; Invalidate below 13 percent for FY2027.
- UK brand revenue: current +3 percent; modal flat to +2 percent; Alarm -3 percent for a half; Invalidate two halves below -3 percent with off-trade share falling.

judgement.markdown:
- **Industry:** A. Consumer staples. Industry RS 33 at the Friday 2 October reading (33 four weeks earlier; 26 on Monday's daily reading)
- **Sector:** A.1. Beverages, beer (where the taxonomy places it). Sector RS 43 at the 30 September month-end (42 four weeks earlier). Its other companies: Carlsberg (Stock RS 47, held), AB InBev (59), Coca-Cola Enterprises (57), Coca-Cola HBC (47), Heineken (42), Royal Unibrew (9), and 1 more
- **Cohort:** non-alcoholic and mixer soft drinks. The cohort's relative strength 48 (12 four weeks earlier), 3 companies: Coca-Cola HBC (47), AG Barr (13)


**What is going on, and why it matters**

- **The price move by beta:** over 5 sessions the stock rose 0.3% to 832p; the market's fall explains -0.9%, so its own move was +1.2%, a third of its usual size (about 3.9%). Over 20 sessions it rose 2.5% while its sector's companies fell 3.8%: an own move of +5.4%, about its usual size
  - No public news explains the week
- **The sector and cohort:** its Stock RS has risen for two months (31 at the end of June, 44 at the end of August, 51 at the month-end) and the cohort's from 12 to 48 in four weeks.
  - The stock is improving inside a sector that is not (Sector RS 43), which is exactly why the third criterion is still met (sector below 50, stock below 70)
- **The analysts:** Net Upgrade Breadth, sales estimates -18% and target prices -7%, unchanged from the end of August: more analysts cutting than raising on both, but with Stock RS 51 above 50 the fourth criterion is not met (both analyst cells are amber); Sell-side Momentum C, from D and F

**What it means for the position**

- **Holding:** held only by your one-off link: two criteria are met (the slope -1.2%; Sector RS 43 with Stock RS 51)
- **Selling:** fifth in the order of sale. Otherwise the 30% level is 617p, 26% below, and the relative 52W high trigger 774p, 7% below, read on 30 October; possible within the quarter, not the base case, because the stock is rising relative to its sector
- **Adding:** not allowed and not wanted
- **Its place in the order of sale:** fifth, because its memo is bullish and its readings are moving away from the triggers. What would move it up:
  - A Friday Industry RS below 30 (a third criterion; plausible, the daily reading is 26), or Stock RS falling below 50 by 30 October (the fourth criterion fires at once, because both analyst counts are already negative; plausible, it reads 51).
  - What would move it down: Stock RS above 70 at a month-end (clears the third); the slope turning positive would need a sustained relative rise from -1.2%. What we lose by waiting: little; the exits are 7% and 26% away

**What we could lose:** about 0.52% of the fund's capital, to the 30% level, the only exit that acts on it under the link (0.14% to the relative 52W high trigger, information only)

**Experiment: which stocks Fevertree's own moves have tracked** (last 3 and 6 months)

- **Currys** (same country of listing): 0.35 and 0.26, moderate
- **AB InBev** (same sector): 0.32 and 0.25, weak
- **Bunzl** (same country of listing): 0.30 and 0.26, weak
- **Mitchells & Butlers** (same country of listing): 0.28 and 0.22, weak
- **My reading:** its moves are mostly its own; a UK consumer factor at most

**The Investment Analyst's memo (digest of 22 September at 873p; memo republished 1 October)**

- **Decided:** bullish; progress to Early-Stage; conviction low, a working hypothesis; gates management C, business quality B, predictability C, trackability B. The case clears the eighteen-month 20% bar at 873p with about 2% to spare, so at 832p with a little more
- **Must happen:** US off-trade scanner growth holds at 10% to 12% through the 2027 financial year (16% in July and August); shipments do not run ahead of scanner sales by more than 5 points; onshoring on time (cans autumn 2026, glass 2027); a 12.4% group margin for 2026
- **Main risk:** the first-half numbers are a false friend: pipeline fill and marketing-bought trial in the visible half of the US business, while the on-trade is commoditised
- **Expected return (the Modal return):** clears our 20% a year bar over eighteen months at 873p by about 2%; the three-year bar only below about 786p
- **Next test:** the monthly Circana scanner data (alarm below 10% for a quarter); the fourth-quarter 2026 US scanner print

**My judgement:** neutral on the position, medium conviction: a holding under the link whose memo is bullish (as Helios Towers' is, and as Theon's and Xvivo's would be at today's prices) and whose relative strength has improved for two months; the two criteria it meets are lagging trend measures

- Sell fifth, and with Helios Towers the best candidate for you to keep by overrule when a purchase reaches it.
- **Counter-case:** the analysts are still cutting on both counts, the industry's relative strength read 33 on Friday and 26 on Monday, and one more weak Friday puts three criteria on it
  - A stock at 19 times forward earnings (the memo's figure) in a sector the market is leaving does not need a thesis to fall 7% relative by month-end and fire a fourth

**What would change my view:** Friday's Industry RS (below 30); the Circana monthly scanner data (below 10%); the 30 October Stock RS (above 70 clears the third; below 50 fires the fourth)
